title: Roasting the change that finally locks the front door

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Welcome back to the spec roast. Today's change has a noble mission: stop family photo albums from being open to the whole internet.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Noble. Overdue. Today, an album link never expires and can't be revoked. Forward it to the wrong group chat and your cousin's coworkers are uploading memes into grandma's birthday album.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Which is exactly what this fixes. Owners can revoke the link, and a new one is issued straight away.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: I'll give it that. One click and the leak is closed. Applause, genuinely.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: And the clever bit: revoking doesn't keep a list of banned links. It just swaps the album's token for a new random one.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Clever, and also a nuclear option. Rotate the token and every link dies, including the one aunt Carmen printed and stuck on her fridge.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: The design calls that acceptable, because rotating is a deliberate owner action.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Deliberate, sure. Until the owner realises the whole family is now locked out and the group chat lights up.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Fair. Next: links also expire. Each token gets an expiry date, and the lifetime comes from configuration.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Lovely. And what is that lifetime?

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: That's… an open question. Seven, thirty or ninety days.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Undecided. And yet the migration already decided: existing links expire thirty days after release. The task list picked a number the design is still debating.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Okay, that one lands. Pick the default first, or derive the migration from it.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Now my favourite line. Owners get an email three days before a link expires, with a button to extend it.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: That's thoughtful.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: It is a button to nowhere. No requirement says links can be extended, and no task builds it. We are emailing people a promise.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Point taken. Either add the requirement and the task, or drop the button.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Then there's the breaking change. Permanent links are removed outright.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: With a migration: old links expire thirty days after release, and owners can issue new ones any time.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Right. Thirty days for every family to notice, in an app whose main channel to them is… an email we haven't built the button for.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Moderation, then. Owners can now delete any photo, whoever uploaded it.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Good. Also permanent. No undo, no record of who deleted what. One tired thumb at midnight and the wedding photos are gone for everyone.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: And one more open question: should people who joined through a revoked link stay in the album?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Because if they stay, revoking the link closes the door after the burglar is already on the sofa.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Last roast, I promise. Rotation, expiry and a data migration all touch who can see what…

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: And the task list has zero tests. Not one. Access control on vibes.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Alright, serious minute. If you're reviewing this change, here's what's on you.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: One: pick the default link lifetime, and make the migration use it.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Two: decide whether members who came in through a revoked link keep their access.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Three: build the extend button, or stop promising it. And add tests while you're at it.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: And say nice things too. Revoking a leaked link in one click is a real improvement. It just needs the rest of the house finished.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Thanks for listening. Go lock your front doors.
